_note: Starting catalogue. Each route links to the official government page. Summaries are deliberately general and marked unverified until a person checks them against the official page (verified_at). Salary thresholds, fees and processing times change often and are NOT stored here: always read the official page. Not legal advice.

routes.name: Skilled Worker visa
routes.summary: For people with a job offer from a UK employer that is an approved (licensed) sponsor, in an eligible occupation. A minimum salary and English language requirement apply.

rules.description: Needs a job offer from an employer approved by the Home Office as a sponsor.
A minimum salary applies and depends on the occupation. Check the official page for current figures.

routes.name: H-1B specialty occupation
routes.summary: For specialty occupations that generally require at least a bachelor's degree or equivalent in a specific field. The US employer files the petition; an annual cap and selection process apply to most employers.

rules.description: A US employer must petition on your behalf.
Generally a bachelor's degree or higher (or equivalent) in a related specific field.

routes.name: Express Entry (skilled immigration)
routes.summary: Points-based system for skilled workers applying for permanent residence. Language test results and skilled work experience are central; a job offer is not always required.

rules.description: Approved English or French language test results are required.
Skilled work experience is assessed; program-specific minimums apply.

routes.name: EU Blue Card (Germany)
routes.summary: For university graduates (or, in some IT roles, experienced professionals) with a qualifying job offer in Germany above a minimum salary. The employer does not need a sponsor licence, but a concrete job offer is required.

rules.description: A recognised university degree, or for some IT roles qualifying professional experience.
A minimum gross salary applies (lower for shortage occupations). Check the official page.
Needs a concrete job offer or employment contract.

routes.name: Highly skilled migrant
routes.summary: The Dutch employer must be a recognised sponsor with the IND and pay at least the applicable salary criterion.

rules.description: Employer must be recognised as a sponsor by the IND.
A salary criterion applies (age-dependent). Check the official page.

routes.name: Critical Skills Employment Permit
routes.summary: For occupations on Ireland's critical skills list, with a job offer from an Irish employer meeting salary and duration conditions.

rules.description: Needs a job offer from an employer in Ireland.
Minimum salary thresholds apply. Check the official page.

routes.name: Skills in Demand visa (subclass 482)
routes.summary: Temporary visa for skilled workers sponsored by an approved Australian employer. Occupation, skills, English and experience requirements apply.

rules.description: Needs sponsorship by an approved Australian employer.
Relevant work experience is required; check the official page for the stream that applies.

routes.name: Employment Pass
routes.summary: For professionals, managers and executives with a job offer in Singapore. The employer applies; a qualifying salary and a points-based assessment (COMPASS) apply.

rules.description: The Singapore employer applies on your behalf.
A qualifying salary applies (higher for some sectors). Check the official page.

routes.name: Employment (work) visa
routes.summary: Residence visas for employment are generally sponsored by the UAE employer. Separate long-term options (for example the Golden Visa) have their own criteria.

rules.description: Usually sponsored by the employer in the UAE.
